name: warm-up ignores zero digits
input: digits with duplicate and zero values
test:
assert smallest_number([4, 1, 4, 2, 3]) == '12344'
assert smallest_number([0, 1, 2]) == '12'
assert smallest_number([0, 2, 5]) == '25'

name: returns the smallest bounded permutation
input: an exact bound plus the corrected and shorter source examples
test:
assert smallest_number([6, 2, 9], 629) == '629'
assert smallest_number([7, 1, 8], 719) == '781'
assert smallest_number([1, 7, 8], 7) == '178'
assert smallest_number([1, 2, 3, 3, 4], 332) == '12334'

name: uses zeros in the follow-up and rejects impossible bounds
input: leading-zero candidates and an overlong bound
test:
assert smallest_number([7, 3, 0, 1], 1) == '1037'
assert smallest_number([0, 0, 4], 20) == '400'
assert smallest_number([1, 2], 30) == '-1'
